name: bugledger-mcp

tools.name: record_bug
tools.description: Record a fixed bug into the local ledger. Call only after the user has confirmed the symptom, root cause, and feature area. Returns the new record id; show it to the user.

symptom.description: What was observed before the fix, e.g. 'login returned 500 when the email had a plus sign'. Not 'fixed auth'.

root_cause.description: WHY it happened: the mechanism that made the failure possible. At least 20 characters. Not the patch, not 'fixed it'.

feature_area.description: Short stable slug used for later lookup: auth, uploads, billing. Reuse an existing slug from list_areas when one fits.

project.description: Repository or package name you are working in, usually the git root directory name.

severity.description: low, medium, or high. Omit if you cannot justify it.

fix_ref.description: Git commit hash of the fix, 7 to 40 hex chars. The server runs `git show` on it to store the diff. Omit if there is no commit yet.

diff_hunk.description: The fix diff itself, used when there is no commit or git show fails. Only the change that made it correct. Capped at 32KB.

source.description: Capture channel: slash (from the /logbug prompt), confirm (you asked and the user confirmed), or import (bulk import from old notes).

tools.name: get_patterns
tools.description: Call this BEFORE planning, writing specs, or implementing anything in a feature area. Returns the newest past bugs for that area, one line each (symptom → root cause), capped at 30 lines. Account for every line in your plan. Bugs resolved for this project are hidden; search_bugs still finds them.

feature_area.description: Feature area slug you are about to work in, e.g. auth, uploads, billing. Call list_areas to see which slugs exist.

project.description: Repository or package name you are working in. Bugs already resolved for this project are hidden.

stack.description: Optional technology to filter by, e.g. python, react. Only bugs matching this technology stack are returned.

limit.description: Maximum records to return, 1 to 30. Default 15.

tools.name: search_bugs
tools.description: Search past bugs by symptom or root cause: 'have we seen this before?'. Use it while debugging. Omit the filters to search the whole ledger, including bugs already resolved for this project.

query.description: Words from an error message, symptom, or root cause. Paste the key part of the error as is: punctuation is ignored, any word may match, and the best matches come first.

feature_area.description: Optional feature area slug to narrow the search.

project.description: Optional project name to narrow the search.

tools.name: list_areas
tools.description: List every feature_area slug and project name in the ledger with record counts. Call it before record_bug or get_patterns to reuse existing names instead of inventing new ones, or to see what the ledger holds.

tools.name: resolve_bug
tools.description: Hide a bug from get_patterns for one project because that project now guards against it: a regression test, a Semgrep rule, or the fix itself is in place. Other projects still see the bug, and search_bugs finds it everywhere.

id.description: Record id from get_patterns, search_bugs, or record_bug, e.g. rec_00042.

project.description: The project that now has a guardrail for this bug.

tools.name: update_bug
tools.description: Correct one or more fields on an existing bug record. Pass only the fields that changed; omitted fields are left as they are.

id.description: Record id from get_patterns, search_bugs, or record_bug, e.g. rec_00042.

root_cause.description: New root cause, at least 20 characters explaining WHY.

stack.description: New technology list, replaces the old one.

fix_ref.description: Git commit hash of the fix, 7 to 40 hex chars.

diff_hunk.description: The fix diff. Use this when record_bug reported diff_source 'none' and you have the change in front of you.

tools.name: delete_bug
tools.description: Permanently delete a bug record and any resolutions tied to it. This cannot be undone; confirm with the user first. To hide a bug for one project instead, use resolve_bug.

id.description: Record id from get_patterns, search_bugs, or record_bug, e.g. rec_00042.

tools.name: get_guardrails
tools.description: Returns the Bug Ledger starter pack of Semgrep rules for classic AI-coding mistakes (injection, hardcoded secrets, unsafe deserialization, open CORS, and more) as files to write into .bugledger/, plus the CI workflow to add. ERROR rules block PRs, WARNING rules are advisory. Never edit existing CI files.

stack.description: Primary language of the project: python, javascript, typescript, ruby, java, go, and so on. Use 'all' for every rule. Language-neutral rules are always included.

instructions:
Bug Ledger is a local memory of bugs this team has already fixed. Use it so the same bug is never written twice.

- Before planning or implementing work in a feature area, call get_patterns(feature_area, project) and account for every returned bug in your plan and code.
- While debugging, call search_bugs with the key words of the error or symptom to check whether it was seen before.
- After a bug is fixed and the user confirms the details, record it with record_bug. The /logbug prompt walks through this. Never record feature work, refactors, or guesses.
- Call list_areas to see which feature_area slugs and project names already exist, and reuse them so records stay findable.
- project is the name of the repository or package you are working in, usually the git root directory name.
